AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 7, 2023
  UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
  ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
 THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
  https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Ana Valencia, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Valencia

INVOCATION
  Pastor Matt Penalber
  New Harvest Church Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Luis Martinez
  Waite Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim March as National Social Services Worker month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to Recognize the Transportation Department’s 2022 Distinguished Coach Operator of the
  Year.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Athens Disposal Update.

  3.  Sprouts Ribbon Cutting Video.

  4.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of February
  21, 2023. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period February 5, 2023 –
  February 18, 2023, in the total amount of $1,068,290.31. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  February 14, 2023 - February 27, 2023, in the total amount of $3,034,779.23. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Alec Borum,
  Anthony Guereque, Interinsurance Exchange of the Automobile Club on behalf of Nelson Munguia, and
  Nelson Munguia. 830-02/07/09/13

  Report

  5.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-18 – DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – PUBLIC SERVICES
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-18, A RESOLUTION OF THE
   CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN
  RECORDS IN THE PUBLIC SERVICES DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  6.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – FEBRUARY 22, 2023 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  7.  REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR CARNIVAL - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the dates requested by the Norwalk Lions Club from Monday, May 22 through Thursday, June
  1, 2023. 920-01-02

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT - INSTALLATION OF MODULAR RESTROOM FOR BOB WHITE PARK – PROJECT
  NO. 7353 - Staff recommends City Council award a contract to Public Restroom Company of Minden,
  Nevada, for the installation of a modular restroom building at Bob White Park, in the amount of
  $187,666.00; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any change orders or
  amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 1005-04-7353

  Report

  9.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT VARIOUS CITY FACILITIES – Staff recommends City Council
  confirm the emergency service repair work on doors at Gerdes, Holifield, Lakeside, and Norwalk parks
  completed by Commercial Door of Los Angeles County, Inc., in the amount of $59,044. 955

  Report

  10. 2022 NORWALK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT - Staff
  recommends City Council receive and file the 2022 General Plan and Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report and direct staff to transmit the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning and
  Research and the California Department of Housing and Community Development prior to April 1,
  2023. 320-02/320-02-03

  Report

  11. AGREEMENT – PUBLIC SAFETY CONSULTANT - Staff recommends City Council approve an
  agreement with Dennis H. Kato, as a Public Safety Consultant, not to exceed $30,000 from March 13,
  2023 through June 30, 2023; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on behalf of
  the City in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  13. PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023/24 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council and the public provide input of the proposed Community
  Development Block Grant and HOME Investment Partnerships Program funding activities for Fiscal
  Year 2023/24 Annual Action Plan. 315

  Report
   14. RESOLUTION NO. 23-14 - ZONE CHANGE NO. 362 TO AMEND THE ZONING DESIGNATION OF
  PORTIONS OF THE SITE ZONED AUTOMOBILE PARKING TO RESTRICTED COMMERCIAL - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-14, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING ZONE CHANGE NO. 362 AND THE ASSOCIATED
  MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING
  PROGRAM. 320-09-362

  Report

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 23-17 - PROPOSED ALLOCATION PLAN FOR THE HOME INVESTMENT
  PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT ENTITLEMENT - Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-17, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE SUBMISSION OF THE HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  PROGRAM AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN. 315

  Report

  16. RESOLUTION NO. 23-15 – SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN AND RESOLUTION NO. 23-16 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – RECEIPT OF HOME
  INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDS - Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 23-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING A SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22
  ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, APPLICATION OF HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM
  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDS AND IMPLEMENTATION OF HOME INVESTMENT
  PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute and transmit all required documents to the United States
  Department of Housing and Urban Development; and

  c.  adopt Resolution No. 23-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ADOPTED BUDGET
  TO APPROPRIATE HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM AMERICAN RESCUE
  PLAN ACT FUNDS FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, in
  the amount of $1,231,940. 315/610

  Report

REPORTS

  17. ART IN PUBLIC PLACES PROJECT APPROVAL – CIVIC CENTER PARKING STRUCTURE MURAL -
  Staff recommends City Council accept the recommendation of the Art in Public Places Committee and
  approve the mural for the Civic Center Parking Structure. 405-01

  Report

  18. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AND FACILITY USE AGREEMENT - Staff recommends City
  Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding from March 2023 to March 2028, for assistance
  with emergency preparedness and response efforts and the Facility Use Agreement with the American
  Red Cross; and authorize the City Manager to execute both documents on behalf of the City, in forms
  approved by the City Attorney. 425-03-01/710/920-03-08/920-06-02/920-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 2, 2023.
 Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk

SYNOPSIS

  REGULAR MEETING
